objectives.title: Hear Eurylochus Out
objectives.hint: He is on the sand beside you, and he will not let this go until you answer him one way or the other.

objectives.title: Find Perimedes
objectives.hint: He is just inside the mouth of the cave, crouched where the stone came down.

obj/the-stone.text: Stone grinds across the mouth, and the daylight narrows to a line, and then to nothing.

objectives.title: Give the Giant a Name
objectives.hint: Polyphemus is deep inside — past the opened stone, past the pens, at the great hearth at the far end. Go and talk to him before you help yourself to anything of his.

obj/the-name.text: The wine does its work. The giant's chin sinks to his chest, and the whole cave fills with the sound of him sleeping.

objectives.title: Cut the Olive Beam
objectives.hint: Past the stone Polyphemus rolled aside, the sheep pens are stacked with his cut timber — the olive beam is in the chest among them.

objectives.title: Grind the Point
objectives.hint: Carry the beam back toward the mouth, near where Perimedes is waiting — the giant keeps a grinding stone there for his own tools.

objectives.title: Harden it in the Fire
objectives.hint: His hearth burns deeper in, beside where he sleeps. Turn the point in the coals until it blackens.

objectives.title: Put Out the Eye
objectives.hint: He went down where the wine took him, at his own hearth. Go back to him with the hardened stake.

obj/blind.text: And the hills answer him. Voices all round the mountain, his own kind, calling in at the stone: 'Polyphemus! What ails you? Is someone killing you? Who is hurting you?' — And he puts his ruined face to the stone and roars back at them with everything he has: 'NOBODY! Nobody is killing me! Nobody is hurting me!' ... A pause. Then, from outside, already moving away: 'If nobody is hurting you, then it is a sickness sent from Zeus, and there is no help for that. Pray to your father.' — And the footsteps go off up the mountain, all of them, and they do not come back. He hears them go.

And the hills answer him. Voices all round the mountain, his own kind, calling in at the stone: 'Polyphemus! Who has done this to you?' — And he sets his ruined face to the stone and roars back a name, whole and proud, the one you laid down over the wine: 'ODYSSEUS! Odysseus, sacker of cities, son of Laertes, of Ithaca — he was under my roof!' — And they take it as true. You hear them come down to the mouth and set their shoulders to the great stone from the outside — and it does not so much as grind, because it is his stone, and only his to move. 'Hold, cousin — we cannot shift it from here. Wait for the light: we come back at dawn, every hand on the mountain, and we open it together.' — And the footsteps go off quick and certain. Perimedes has your sleeve, low and fast: 'They come back at dawn, Captain. We leave with the flock before they do.'

And the hills answer him. Voices all round the mountain, his own kind, calling in at the stone: 'Polyphemus! Who has done this to you?' — And he sets his ruined face to the stone and roars back the name you gave him over the wine: 'AITHON! A Cretan, Aithon, out of Crete — he was under my roof, at my own fire!' — A silence. Then, from outside, cool and already turning away: 'A Cretan. — Cousin, the Cretans lie; it is the one thing every man knows of them. And now the liars are indoors with you, are they, and the stone still shut from the inside. ... Sleep it off.' — And the footsteps go, unhurried, half-convinced of nothing, and they do not come back tonight. He stands in the dark with a false name ringing off his walls and no one at all coming to his hurt.
Get out of the cave. Make no sound he can follow.

objectives.title: Get Under a Ram
objectives.hint: Leave him roaring at his hearth and slip in among the flock down the cavern from him — get underneath a ram and take hold of the fleece, and let it carry you out past his hands. Do not run and do not jump; he hunts by sound now.

objectives.title: Go Out With the Flock
objectives.hint: Perimedes is waiting back at the mouth of the cave, in among the rams. Get to him before the flock is through.

obj/the-ram.text: Two fistfuls of wool, close in at the belly where it is thickest. The ram walks, and you walk out under it.

objectives.title: The Ship Is Waiting
objectives.hint: Eurylochus is at the water's edge with the oars manned. Tell him how you want to leave.

effects.text: You set your shoulder to the great stone. It does not so much as grind. No blade you carry will bite it — whatever opens this cave, it will not be you.
